chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed three distinct Umras: an Umra in Dhi al-Qadah, entering into ihram from Usfan, and this is the Umra of Al-Hudaybiyya; and an Umra entering into ihram from Al-Juhfa, and this is the Umra of Qaza (compensation); and an Umra entering into ihram from Al-Ji'rana after returning from Al-Ta'if from the expedition of Hunayn.

key_terms.حُنَيْنٍ: Hunayn (a valley and historical battle site)

ai.seo_question: What are the three distinct Umras performed by the Prophet Muhammad and their corresponding locations of ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi clarifies the historical sequence of the Prophet’s three Umras, distinguishing the Umra of Al-Hudaybiyya, the compensatory Umra of Qaza, and the post-Hunayn Umra from Al-Ji'rana. Shia scholars utilize this account to establish the Sunnah of performing Umra independently of Hajj and to validate the specific miqat locations associated with each pilgrimage, reinforcing the jurisprudential understanding of the Prophet’s ritual practices.
